input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

errors.what: First CI run of PR #16481 red in changed-ventures: repair-flow.test.mjs 'repair reserve on by default from 300 copies' (merged from main via PR #16466) got null; budget-starved at 3 s on a loaded runner. Reproduced locally 4/4 under load; fixed forward with a 10 s budget on the big week.

doc_friction.issue: 'Where to look' item 2 points at ci_profile.py, but platform/ci/venture_suite_times.json (per-suite times, refreshed by run_venture_tests.py --write-times) answered 'which suite' with no runner reading; worth naming there.
optimality.openRow.bound is reported from cgRow.floor, not cgRow.bound; my first seeded fault set the wrong field and looked like a missed catch.

deviations.why: 'Never drop, skip or weaken a test' read strictly would bar shortening a budget in a test. I shortened exactMs only for a phase the test does not check, and kept the checks it does make.
deviations.did: Showed that both stopped passes still run on all 6 calls at 300 ms, added a direct assertion on the open-hours row's bound, and planted a fault in each bound to show it is still caught.
deviations.result: Test 2 went from 59 s to 13 s and still catches both planted faults.

notes: Metric: wall time of shift-roster-builder cg-hardstop.test.mjs, from `node --test --test-reporter=tap cg-hardstop.test.mjs` run alone on 4 cores, twice each way (git stash for before). Test 2: 58.9 s and 59.5 s before, 13.1 s and 13.0 s after. Whole file: 75.8 s and 77.1 s before, 30.2 s and 29.8 s after, about 46 s of CPU saved per suite run. The per-file reading of all 70 files (4 at a time) found calc.test.mjs 105 s, cg-hardstop 81 s, open-sums 54 s, cover-guide 33 s. cover-guide test 3 was checked: its time is in coverPass/coverRepair, the subject under test, so it was left alone. Suite run: python3 platform/ci/run_venture_tests.py shift-roster-builder, ok (237.0 s, 663 tests, 0 failed) on this container, run alone. Also fixed forward main's repair-flow reserve test (5.5 s flaky to 14.6 s stable, 4/4 at 4x load), so the net is about -37 s CPU per suite run.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an engineer timing 70 test files, profiling phases, checking budget equivalence with seeded faults, and writing it up

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
